content:
Some experiences go beyond textbooks and classrooms—they allow you to witness the legal system more closely, interact with professionals, and understand how the concepts we study actually operate in practice.
As part of an educational visit to Delhi from 7–10 September 2026, I had the opportunity to visit some of India’s most significant legal institutions, including The Supreme Court of India, Indian Law Institute and the Law Commission of India.
We began with a visit to the Indian Law Institute, where we attended an insightful session by Dr. Rajesh Kumar The session was an engaging and interactive one, which gave us the opportunity to discuss our questions and gain perspectives beyond what we encounter in our regular coursework. I am very thankyou to Dr. Rajesh Kumar for giving us time and interact with us.
We then visited the Supreme Court of India, where we had the privilege of interacting with Advoacte on Record Kunal Yadav and Dr. Anu Bhuvanachandran. I am sincerely thankful to them for giving us their valuable time. Visiting the Court in person was particularly meaningful as a law student. We also got the opportunity to explore the library and witness important constitutional and legal resources, making the experience even more enriching.
Day 2 took us to Law Commission Of India where we attended an informative session by Prof. D. P. Verma on the role and functioning of the Commission. The interactive discussion with Dr. Anju Rathi Rana Mam and Deeba Ashraf was one of the highlights of the visit. What made the session especially valuable was how openly our questions were addressed, giving us a much clearer understanding of the Commission’s work, law reform, research, and its contribution to the development of Indian law.
What I appreciated most throughout the visit was the constant encouragement from our faculty, who encouraged us to ask questions, engage in discussions and make the most of every interaction. The willingness of the professionals and faculty members we met to listen to our questions and share their experiences made the visit genuinely insightful. I am grateful to Dr. Shafia Shah and Dr. Mohd Aqib Aslam for their guidance, encouragement and support throughout the visit.
Finally, sincerely thankful to Prof. Ankur Gupta, Director, MIET and School of Law, MIET for this great opportunity.
This visit gave me more than institutional exposure—it gave me a closer perspective on the functioning of the legal system and the many dimensions of a career in law. I look forward to carrying these insights forward in my academic and professional journey.
Grateful for the experience, the conversations, and the learning beyond the classroom.

comment: Institutional visits are most valuable when students connect courtroom processes, legal research, and policy-making. That bridge between theory and practice often shapes how future lawyers approach problems beyond the classroom.
